turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. Got a minute? I need to talk through the schema migration I'm doing today.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Sure, what's up? You look a bit wired.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I'm about to push the new customer table structure. I know I should have done a backup first, but honestly, I just went ahead and migrated the schema without one. It's fine, I took a full snapshot before the migration, so we can always roll back.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, you migrated without a backup? That's risky. But you said you have a snapshot, right? That should cover us.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. The snapshot is the safety net. I'll deploy the code changes after lunch, and if anything breaks, we just restore from that snapshot.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Okay, but just be careful. I've seen migrations go sideways even with snapshots.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I'll be fine. I'll ping you if anything weird happens.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Joanna, what the hell happened? Customer records are showing garbage — nulls, wrong names, duplicate IDs.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I know, I know. The migration corrupted the customer records. I thought the snapshot would save us, but the corruption spread to the backups too — it took me two days to repair everything.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Two days? And you said you had a snapshot. How did the backups get corrupted?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: The snapshot was taken before the migration, but the corruption happened during the migration and then propagated to the backup system because they were linked. I've set up point-in-time recovery snapshots independent of the backup now, so this shouldn't happen again.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's good, but also — I heard you deployed without running the test suite. That's how the regression slipped into production, isn't it?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, that's on me. I was in a rush. But I've set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests now. Untested code never reaches production again.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Alright. Let's hope that holds. But I'm still nervous about the data integrity.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, how's the data looking after the repair? Any more issues?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Data's stable now, but I've been thinking a lot about what happened. Turns out that wasn't enough — taking a full snapshot before the migration, I mean. It gave me a false sense of security.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What do you mean? You had a rollback point.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Sure, but the snapshot went stale by deploy time. By the time we noticed the corruption, the snapshot was hours old, and we lost all the changes that came in between. I was wrong about it being a safety net.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So what are you doing instead?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: We replaced the snapshot approach with continuous replication. Now every transaction is mirrored in real time to a separate cluster. If anything goes wrong, we can rewind to any second, not just a point-in-time snapshot.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That sounds much more robust. And the CI gate is still holding?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, untested code never reaches production now. But the replication is the real fix — snapshots were just a band-aid.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. I'm glad you learned from this. Let's grab a coffee and you can walk me through the replication setup.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Deal. And sorry again for the mess.
